College Examiner Viva Q&A & Theoretical Architecture
Q1: Why is Tabular Q-Learning chosen over Deep Q-Networks (DQN)? +
Tabular Q-Learning provides 100% explainability, mathematical transparency, and deterministic reproducibility. For a college examination, every state-action pair $Q(s, a)$ can be inspected directly in a table, proving that decisions are driven by exact Bellman updates rather than black-box neural network approximations. Furthermore, training converges in under 30 seconds on a standard CPU with zero heavy dependencies (no PyTorch, no TensorFlow).
Q2: How does parameter sharing work across the 4 autonomous vehicles? +
Rather than maintaining 4 separate Q-tables, all 4 vehicles share a single common Q-table $(324 \times 6)$. Whenever any vehicle becomes idle, it queries this shared table using its local state $s = (v_{\text{quad}}, b_0, b_1, b_2, b_3)$. Transitions experienced by all 4 vehicles update the same table. This speeds up sample efficiency by $4\times$ and guarantees that the entire fleet adheres to a unified operational policy.
Q3: What makes this a Semi-Markov Decision Process (SMDP)? +
Standard MDPs assume that every action takes exactly 1 discrete time step. However, dispatching an autonomous vehicle involves variable-duration macro-actions: traveling to pickup and traveling to dropoff takes $\Delta t$ time steps depending on Manhattan distance. Under the SMDP formulation, the Bellman optimality equation discounts the future state by $\gamma^{\Delta t}$: $$Q(s, a) \leftarrow Q(s, a) + \alpha \left[ \sum_{k=0}^{\Delta t - 1} \gamma^k r_k + \gamma^{\Delta t} \max_{a'} Q(s', a') - Q(s, a) \right]$$ This properly balances short trips against long repositioning maneuvers.
Q4: Why does the Nearest-Vehicle Baseline fail during demand surges? +
Greedy nearest-dispatch operates with myopic spatial bias: it repeatedly dispatches available vehicles to newly spawned nearby requests in the hotspot core, starving requests on the periphery. Those starved passengers accumulate wait time until they hit the 60-step cancellation threshold, causing heavy penalties and lost revenue. In contrast, the RL agent uses state awareness to balance nearest service with longest-waiting priority and proactive repositioning.
